EXTRACTION FINDING: This section contains ONLY executive compensation decisions and awards. There are NO SIFI-material entities, relationships, or risk signals. NO material counterparty relationships, hidden leverage, circularity, capex commitments to AI labs, investments in private AI companies, off-balance-sheet entities, or customer/supplier concentration > 10% are disclosed in this section. IBM's Gen AI initiatives (Granite 3.0 & 3.1, Qiskit) are internal product development, not SIFI-material counterparty arrangements. CONCLUSION: No SIFI-material extraction warranted. Return minimal graph with only IBM as filer context."

[chunk 4/5] IBM DEF 14A filing (2025-03-10) - Beneficial Owners section contains minimal SIFI-material content. The proxy statement is primarily procedural (voting instructions, executive compensation, stockholder proposals on lobbying and DEI). Key entities identified: (1) Audit supplier PwC ($72.6M annual fees) with 67-year tenure creates switching cost but no leverage risk; (2) Kyndryl separation (Nov 2021) of Managed Infrastructure business noted for revenue comparability; (3) Vote tabulation and transfer agent dependencies are operational but routine; (4) Lobbying disclosure shows IBM is member of Business Roundtable and US Chamber of Commerce but the proposal disputes the transparency and alignment of these relationships. No hidden leverage, circularity, or SIFI-material concentration risk detected in this section. The stockholder proposals (Proposals 4 and 5) are reputational/governance issues, not financial stability risks. Per HARD RULE 3, skipping boilerplate on generic market risks and routine governance matters."
[chunk 5/5] This DEF 14A proxy filing is primarily administrative and procedural, focused on shareholder meeting logistics, proxy voting procedures, and householding disclosure. The material SIFI-relevant extractions are limited: (1) the FX hedging SPV for the StreamSets/webMethods acquisition from Software AG, which was marked-to-market through 2024 with a $68M loss impact; (2) IBM's significant pension settlement and transfers to insurers ($3.1B charge in 2024, $7B in obligations transferred), creating cost-opacity and potential off-balance-sheet leverage; (3) routine vendor dependencies (Computershare, Broadridge, Innisfree M&A). The Kyndryl spinoff and Red Hat acquisition are referenced in financial reconciliations but no novel counterparty risk or circularity is evident in this section. No AI lab relationships or customer/supplier concentration > 10% of revenue are named. Generative AI book of business is mentioned as consulting-focused but no SIFI-material contract or capex commitment is disclosed."
